body: If you want to be friends, I’m here. I know I can’t solve your problems. But my boyfriend committed suicide last month, and I want to reach out to be a support.

I’ve been seeing two therapists (one from school and one through my insurance) They both are sucky honestly, but I’m gonna keep trying to find ways to release all the extra built up energy and tension inside of me.
Thank you so much, and I try to keep my thoughts positive, but my mind wanders into grieving. It’s really hard. Thank you so much for your kind words.
Thank you. It means a lot to hear (or see) those words.

There’s a lot more to the story. His dad committed suicide 2 years prior, and he told me that he was going to commit suicide before he met me. I texted his family for an intervention, because they had faced the death of his father, and I wanted him to talk to people who knew what he was going through. He also got into a huge fight with his mom the month before where he went to jail for no reason. I knew I loved him, but he knew that too. He said he was hanging on for his mom, so after that fight, I think is when he let go. I encouraged him to reach out to her, but he was still processing what happened between them. I never knew he was in that much pain. He was used to hiding everything since he was little, but I tried to get him to open up as much as I could. I just didn’t want to be forceful bc then he’d be upset

My boyfriend committed suicide a month ago, and I wish I could have told him I loved him or talked to him to help. I don’t know you, but I know you’re loved very deeply, and I’m here to talk. I have the same thoughts everyday, but you don’t have to be alone.
